Fix id remapping at deserialisation, using serialisation context
selection using thread locals.
This isn't ideal, but is the least intrusive fix I've come up with.
The serialisation context for a thread of execution is set by creating
a serialisation context instance, and using a ContextGuard instance to
set is as the current context.
The context is set for the scope of the ContextGuard instance,
so use in a fashion similar to lock_guards.
Stop passing around serialisation context pointers.
Remap ids as deserialisation using the current serialisation context.
Add test program exp2.cpp to check ID remapping.

If define SSTRING_HAS_DEFAULT_CONTEXT is defined then a default serialisation
context is created and used as the initial value for all threads.
So it is possible to work using a single serialisation context without using
ContextGuards

For songs_db we don't use this, as we want to serialise all strings with each
removable storage location.

More changes to handle removable storage correctly. Refactor interfaces which take a filepath to use two path components instead of the "absolute" file path.
The first component is the absolute root path, and the second the relative file path.
Audio file information is stored in containers which are now keyed off the relative file path,
and serializations only stores the keys which are relative filepaths.
So serializations stored removable storage are correctly deserialized into live data,
even if the mount point changes.
Unfortunately this means that the impls of AudioFileRecord need access to some root path,
which is stored in impls of AudioFileRecordStore.
The alternative would be to store more strings at the AudioFileRecord impl.
Solved for now at the impls using multiple inheritance and a pointer to runtime Context, which has to be set at deserialization.
